sections.html: Aequidens superomaculatum was scientifically described only in 2015. Unique in the genus, and giving the species its name (superomaculatum = with a spot above), is the combination of a continuous lateral stripe and a lateral spot positioned far above. In the other Aequidens species the lateral stripe is either interrupted or/and the lateral spot is located in the middle of the longitudinal band.

The imported fish are probably Ae. superomaculatum, but some more research is needed before the name of this cichlid can be certain. The new imports differ from the first description specimens in that they have two side spots: the eponymous one below the dorsal fin and additionally one within the longitudinal band. They thus show a striking similarity to the still scientifically undescribed Ae. sp. "Jenaro Herrera" from Peru, found near Jenaro Herrera on the Rio Ucayali. The occurrences of the two are a good 500 km apart as the crow flies. Ae. diadema from the Rio Negro in Venezuela is also very similar and also fits geographically.
Typical of Aequidens, the fish are reserved and somewhat shy.
According to Uwe Werner, it is a larvophilous mouthbrooder: the fish spawns like an open brooder on a solid object as an adhesive spawner and takes the hatched larvae into the mouth for further care.

According to the first description the fish can become about 15 cm long (the largest specimen available to the describers was 133.8 mm without caudal fin). The new imports look particularly attractive because of orange markings that frame the side spot within the longitudinal band and decorate the back.
